transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-11-30 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~48 minutes (recorded)
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (VenturePulse PM), Priya Singh (VenturePulse SRE), Jordan Miles (VenturePulse CTO)

Summary:
This was the weekly pilot scrub focused on throughput tuning. We reviewed last week's metrics from the staging pilot (batching behaviour, mean batch size vs max cap, p95/p99 latency under sustained QPS), tried a quick live retune on the batch cap and concurrency, and agreed a short soak/bench plan. Customer flagged production-like burst patterns at ~2x baseline and wanted conservative fallback thresholds. Also touched briefly on VPC/networking checks and SSO audit requirements.

Topics covered:
- Observed throughput and latency slides from staging runs
- Continuous batching parameters: batch_cap, batch_window, dynamic batching behavior
- Concurrency and inflight controls: max_concurrency, queue depth, backpressure
- Queueing artifacts and transient spikes; headroom/soak tests
- Security and deployment notes: VPC egress, SSO, audit logs for Private pilot

Action items (recap): see metadata action_items field above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: ok, hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll get started. quick round of intros?
[00:16] Alex: hi alex here, product, im mostly watching perf and acceptance criteria for the pilot.
[00:22] Priya: priya, SRE, i'll be running the traces and the traffic shaping for the soak.
[00:28] Jordan: jordan, CTO, short on time but want to see risk posture for the dedicated path.
[00:35] Liam: cool, i'm liam on infra, i'll walk through the numbers we ran yesterday.

[01:05] Liam: so real quick, staging run summary - baseline steady QPS was 220 rps, we see mean batch size around 48 tokens requests per batch, actually around 48 requests per batch, with batch cap at 64. p95 latency was 310ms, p99 at 920ms. when we introduced short spikes to 450 rps we saw queueing increase and p99 hit 1.7s.
[01:42] Alex: that 1.7 s p99 is kinda the sticking point for UX, we want p99 under 1.2s ideally. what were the largest batches during the spike?
[01:55] Liam: they hit cap a few times - batches near 64, but effective batch windows collapsed because of concurrency limits, so more inflight small batches rather than fewer large ones, which hurt throughput.
[02:18] Priya: quick q: is the kv cache being warmed correctly? i saw cold starts in the CSV.
[02:25] Liam: good call. we had a mismatch in the warmup policy - the prefetched prefix was off by one char so some requests missed KV cash - sorry - KV cache. that added token overhead on a subset of requests. we fixed the policy mid-run.

[03:05] Maya: thanks. so the two knobs we tried in this call were bumping batch_cap and increasing max_concurrency, right?
[03:12] Liam: yeah, we moved batch_cap from 64 to 128 and max_concurrency from 16 to 24 on staging, keeping batch_window at 15ms. we observed mean batch size jumped to ~72 and p95 improved to 260ms under steady load, p99 down to 700ms. but under spike to 500 rps the p99 still went to 1.3s, which is better but not perfect.
[03:45] Alex: so bumping cap helped steady flow but spikes still cause queue buildup. what about backpressure thresholds?
[03:53] Liam: currently we've got queue_depth soft limit at 200 and hard limit at 400. once soft is exceeded we reduce batching window, and after hard we fail fast and fallback to a smaller model. that fallback path is configured but hasn't been exercised fully.
[04:20] Jordan: fallback to smaller model is ok if quality tradeoff is acceptable, what are the perf numbers on the smaller variant?
[04:28] Liam: smaller model reduces latency p99 to about 450ms under spike but the generation quality drops, obviously. we can tune the decision rule to only fallback if p99 > 1.5s for more than 30s.

[05:10] Priya: any network issues observed? i want to make sure VPC egress and pod to pod is not the bottleneck.
[05:17] Liam: we ran netperf in parallel, negligible network saturation, all bottlenecks look compute/queuing. we did see one AZ variance - one node had slower NVMe, probably unrelated to Redwood.

[06:00] Maya: ok let's talk about tests we agreed to run this week. liam?
[06:08] Liam: plan A - 12 hour headroom soak on staging with new batch_cap=128 and max_concurrency=24, ramping QPS in steps with 10 minute holds. capture p95/p99, batch size histogram every minute. plan B - synthetic burst replay using customer trace to reproduce 2x spike pattern. we also want an on-prem bench to validate VPC path with realistic egress rules.
[06:40] Alex: for the burst replay, we'll hand over a 24h trace slice. priya will upload.
[06:46] Priya: yep uploading shortly - i'll include the spike markers and sample headers.

[07:20] Speaker 2: small note, from cost side, raising batch cap reduces per-token overhead but increases memory pressure per worker; we should watch OOMs.
[07:33] Liam: yep, we monitored memory, these changes increased peak GPU memory by ~2.5GB, still within margin for our current instance class. if we go further we may need to switch to the next GPU SKU or enable quantizashun - was that spelling, sorry - quantization.

[08:12] Alex: what about dynamic batching logic, any heuristics to prefer larger batches when tail latency allows?
[08:20] Liam: we have a scoring function that accounts for request age and estimated latency. current heuristic weights age higher at very high QPS which fragments batches. we can tweak weights to bias towards larger batches while letting some requests wait up to an extra 20ms in order to group. we tried 20ms bias in one sub-run and saw mean batch size go up by 15% with p95 unchanged.

[09:05] Maya: note to customer, that bias is a tunable we can expose via the console and recommend starting conservative.

[10:00] Priya: when you ramp concurrency how do you avoid head-of-line blocking?
[10:06] Liam: we maintain per-worker inflight queues and round-robin scheduling across model shards. head-of-line can happen if a single request pins a shard; we use request preemption at 2s to avoid long tail blocking. we set preempt to be rare.

[11:12] Jordan: any reliability tradeoffs we should document? i.e. can the system degrade gracefully under repeated spikes?
[11:20] Maya: yes, fallback paths and region fallback are part of the plan. we also have automatic model variant fallback and a circuit-breaker that will scale back concurrency before failing open. we'll add that to the playbook.

[12:00] Liam: quick demo - i pushed the batch_cap change live for a quick 10 minute window to show behaviour. noticed one anomaly: during a specific request pattern the batcher created many small batches due to content-based batching key variance (we group by prompt type), some requests had appended metadata that changed the key.
[12:35] Alex: that sounds like a data issue, we can normalize headers.
[12:40] Priya: we'll do that normalization on our side for the pilot traffic.

[13:10] Maya: switching gears - cost implication: rough estimate, raising batch cap to 128 reduced per-response token cost by ~8% in our sim for their workload, but adding concurrency increases instance hours by about 12%. we'll send updated spreadsheet.

[14:00] Liam: also, for true headroom we want to run the soak overnight with the customer replay so we can see longer tail behavior and cache warmup dynamics.

[15:20] Alex: curious about telemetry; what will you provide?
[15:25] Liam: we'll share a zip: minute-level metrics CSV (p50,p95,p99,mean batch size, queue depth), batch histograms, sample traces and raw logs for any 500/timeout events. link will be posted in the pilot folder.

[16:05] Priya: can you ensure logs include request IDs so we can join with our traces?
[16:10] Liam: yes request-id included.

[17:00] Jordan: security quick Q - SSO and audit logs for the Private deployment? we need proof points for our compliance team.
[17:07] Maya: we have SOC2 report, SAML SSO guides, and an audit log sample. i'll share the security pack link.

[18:00] Alex: perfect. back to tuning - what thresholds do you propose for triggering fallback?
[18:08] Liam: propose a 30s sustained p99 > 1.5s trigger, with soft degradation (reduce batch_window) before hard fallback to smaller model; also a queue_depth soft at 250 to start throttling new requests.

[19:20] Priya: sounds reasonable. can we also get a synthetic test that simulates a 3 minute spike to validate trigger behaviour?
[19:27] Liam: yes, we'll add that to the soak plan.

[20:10] Maya: ok, let's do a quick live retune now and observe a few minutes - liam you want to drive?
[20:16] Liam: toggling batch_cap to 128 now on staging A. give it a minute -
[20:38] Alex: seeing batch size climb to ~70 in the dashboard, p95 trending down to ~250ms.
[20:52] Priya: i also see an increase in outstanding inflight on worker-3 up to 22, which is close to the limit.
[21:05] Liam: good catch, i'll nudge max_concurrency down to 20 on that node to spread load.
[21:18] Speaker 3: small hiccup, one request timed out during the change, it was retried.
[21:25] Liam: noted, retry succeeded.

[22:00] Maya: that live change confirms our earlier sims but also reveals node variance; we'll mark that to address in the runbook.

[23:10] Alex: how do we interpret batch histograms for production -- what upper bound should we expect?
[23:18] Liam: for their workload we'd expect mean batch size 60-90 under steady, 40-60 under spikes if no bias is applied. with bias we can push steady to 85. but this fluctuates by prompt length distribution.

[24:30] Priya: i'll want to see the per-prompt-length breakdown in the CSV.
[24:36] Liam: will include it.

[25:10] Jordan: about fallback, is there a way to route only a small percentage of requests to fallback for canarying?
[25:18] Liam: yes canary routing by percent is available, we can start at 2% and escalate. that's what we typically do to measure quality impact.

[26:05] Alex: on the quality front, do you have any eval harness to compare variants?
[26:12] Maya: we can run a small eval set they provide across both variants and include metrics and sample outputs in the deck.

[27:00] Priya: networking check again - do you need peering to our internal services for tracing?
[27:06] Liam: no peering required for pilot, we'll use signed requests over VPC egress; if they want direct peering we can discuss in next phase.

[28:00] Maya: ok we're approaching the last third of the call, recap of decisions: do the 12h soak, run burst replay, tune queue_depth and fallback thresholds we discussed, share spreadsheets and security pack.

[28:30] Alex: agreed. one more question - any quick wins to reduce p99 now?
[28:36] Liam: quick wins: normalize request headers to reduce batching key variance, bump batch_cap, and slightly bias batch window. we've already seen p99 improve after the live change.

[29:10] Priya: i'll prioritize header normalization, should be quick.

[30:00] Speaker 1: there's also a note to check model kv warmup policy so cold prefixes dont cause spikes.
[30:08] Liam: yep fixed that in config and re-ran a micro test.

[31:20] Alex: what about monitoring for customer side - what dashboards will you give?
[31:26] Maya: per-route latency, batch histograms, queue depth, and a heatmap of batch keys. we'll grant view-only access to their SREs.

[32:15] Priya: can we get alerting thresholds as part of the playbook?
[32:20] Liam: yes we'll propose alert thresholds (p99, queue_depth, and error rate) and include example pager rules.

[33:05] Jordan: timeline check - when do we expect to validate these changes and present to execs?
[33:12] Maya: if soak and replay go as planned, we can assemble results and present a short findings deck by 2026-12-07.

[34:00] Alex: that timeline works.

[34:30] Maya: any other blockers?
[34:35] Priya: none, just need the shared drive instructions.

[35:00] Liam: i'll post the link after the call: https://redwood.app/drive/pilot/venturepulse-bench-11-30 (contains CSVs and runbook).

[36:20] Alex: nice. one last item - cost modeling for Dedicated vs Hosted at scale, can you update the spreadsheet with the new concurrency assumptions?
[36:28] Maya: yep we'll update cost sheet and annotate assumptions per-scenario.

[37:00] Priya: for compliance, i'll loop in our security lead after you share the SOC2 and SAML docs.

[38:10] Maya: will do.

[39:00] Liam: last technical note: we recommend running a 3 minute synthetic spike test in the soak to validate fallback triggers. we'll include that step in the procedure.

[40:00] Alex: good.

[41:05] Speaker 2: small aside - competitor note, a vendor we evaluated had strong default batching heuristics but less observability; we prefer full metric visibility.

[41:30] Jordan: ok, thanks for the thoroughness.

[42:10] Maya: recap of next steps: liam runs soak and posts CSV, priya uploads trace, maya shares security pack and cost sheet, jordan confirms stakeholders.

[43:00] Alex: thanks all. we'll meet same time next week unless something pops.

[44:00] Priya: thanks.
[44:05] Liam: thanks everyone.

[47:30] Maya: meeting end, logging notes. bye.

End of transcript.
